front.title: Poll and Push Modes for HTTP Subscriptions

abstract.t:
In the stream mode of Braid-HTTP subscriptions, the server holds one response open, and sends each change in it. Some origin servers can't hold a response open, such as those that run as serverless functions or on shared hosting. And on some paths, a proxy buffers each response until it ends. This document defines two subscription modes in which nothing stays open for long. In the long-poll mode, the client sends a GET for each change, and the server responds to it when the change happens. In the webhook mode, the origin server pushes each change to a subscription gateway as a PUT or a DELETE, and the gateway serves the subscription to its clients. In both, each message after the first says which version it builds on, and the first can too, so no message depends on a connection, and each can take its own path.
This document is one of the Braid-HTTP extensions, which work alone or together; together they make HTTP a state synchronization protocol.
